name: Petroleum Engineering
boundaries: Petroleum Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Universal enhanced oil recovery above 80 to 90 percent in any reservoir type
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in parts, not added as one concept. Conventional rock is PET-02. Shale matrix is PET-05. Immobile bitumen is PET-09. One fluid for all three would still have to pass three different demonstrations.

original_dispositions.original_title: Real-time meter-scale four-dimensional imaging of a whole field
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by PET-08. The meter-scale full-field clause was not adopted. Time-lapse seismic and fiber already exist at coarser scale or near the well.

original_dispositions.original_title: In-situ molecular upgrading of heavy oil and bitumen to pipeline-quality crude
original_dispositions.reason: Added as PET-11, narrowed to pipeline specification without diluent on a commercial pattern. The emissions percentage was dropped.

original_dispositions.original_title: Zero-discharge produced-water management and mineral valorization
original_dispositions.reason: Reinjection, recycling, and disposal already support current drilling. Mineral recovery from brine is a processing industry. The petroleum-engineering limit that disposal can hit, induced earthquakes, is PET-10. A universal zero-discharge plant does not change reservoir physics.

original_dispositions.original_title: Perfect full-field simulation with error below 5 percent
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by PET-01. The 5 percent figure was not adopted.

original_dispositions.original_title: A net-zero platform for all upstream operations using existing infrastructure
original_dispositions.reason: Halsey and coauthors place leak detection at high technology readiness. The remaining work is deployment, power supply, and site-by-site storage, not one missing petroleum-engineering principle. Storage assurance, where it is a subsurface prediction problem, sits in PET-08 and PET-10.

original_dispositions.original_title: Universal downhole gas-to-liquids or gas-to-power at high efficiency
original_dispositions.reason: Routine flaring is reduced by gathering, reinjection, and surface equipment where those are built. A downhole chemical plant is not required for that, and no result inspected here shows a wellbore converter as a new production regime.

original_dispositions.original_title: Autonomous drilling with zero nonproductive time and a 50 to 70 percent cost cut
original_dispositions.reason: Factory drilling has already cut shale-well costs inside rotary practice, as the 2016 EIA cost study records. The depth and hard-rock penalty that rotary practice has not removed is PET-07. A further cut in ordinary nonproductive time is incremental operations work. The quoted percentage was not found in a primary source.

original_dispositions.original_title: Permanent carbon-dioxide storage guaranteed at 99.9 percent, with a 15 to 25 percent oil-recovery bonus in any reservoir
original_dispositions.reason: Carbon-dioxide enhanced oil recovery and dedicated geologic storage are operating practices, not undiscovered principles. A numerical guarantee for every reservoir type was not found. Plume and fault prediction, where still open, are PET-08 and PET-10.

original_dispositions.original_title: A new class of equipment for sustained production above 30,000 psi and 500 °F
original_dispositions.reason: Anchor has produced since 2024 with 20,000 psi equipment at about 250 °F and reservoir pressures in the mid-20,000 psi range. That is the realized pressure step. The stated 30,000 psi and 500 °F duty is a further rating. It was not shown to be a separate resource revolution beyond PET-07’s depth-and-time problem and the equipment class already in service.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-01: Kept. Stated that the historical “less than 5 percent error” figure is not an authoritative criterion. Noted that the 2026 Darcy-fidelity article is abstract-only and from a minor venue. Pointed shale and bitumen at PET-05 and PET-09 so the simulator claim is not asked to do their work.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical numerical threshold was not a published standard; shale and bitumen are separate barriers.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-02: Kept. Narrowed the wording so one universal chemical for shale and bitumen is explicitly outside this entry. Physics, numbers, and sources are unchanged.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical universal-chemical wish bundles different barriers.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-03: Kept. Noted that the Boswell and Collett passage is from the abstract record, and that the Alaska rate quote was not re-downloaded.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Preserve the limitations of source access.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-04: Kept. No new commercial Green River project was found. No technical change.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The notes report no later commercial project found.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-05: Kept. No technical change. Gas-flow papers remain labeled as gas, not oil, evidence.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Preserve the scope of the evidence.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-06: Kept. Replaced the incorrect “Songhai Qin” attribution with Yuan, Afanasev, Askarova, Popov, and Cheremisin, DOI 10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.125219. Added Hou and coauthors for the temperature ranges. Flagged the boundary with PET-11.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Correct the attribution, support the temperature ranges, and distinguish hydrogen production from liquid upgrading.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-07: Kept. Added Anchor, first oil in 2024 at a 20,000 psi rating and about 250 °F reservoir temperature, so the achieved pressure step is not described as future work. Stated that autonomous zero-nonproductive-time drilling and a further 30,000 psi / 500 °F rating are not this entry.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Distinguish the achieved pressure equipment class and other historical targets from the drilling-time claim.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-08: Kept. Rejected meter-scale full-field coverage as a requirement, because it overstates what seismic wavelengths can do. Cited the 2016 SPE imaging challenge as the historical ancestor. The capability remains blind-well permeability and saturation.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Retain the measurement capability without the unsupported resolution requirement.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-09: Kept. Corrected SPE-50410-MS authors to Ashok K. Singhal, Yoshiaki Ito, and Mahnaz Kasraie. Removed the mistaken attachment of the 1996 SPE-37144 author list. Flagged PET-11 as the separate upgrading claim.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Correct the citation and distinguish native-temperature mobility from upgrading.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-10: Kept. Limited the Groningen statement to the June 2023 cabinet decision. Did not assert that site demolition was independently re-verified. Noted produced-water disposal as one application of the same bound.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Preserve the limit of the Groningen verification and the scope of the pressure-plan concept.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PET-11: Added. The historical in-situ upgrading item is a real gap once it is cut down to pipeline-specification crude from a commercial pattern. Whitesands and CAPRI show partial thermal upgrading and a catalytic add-on that was not continued. The entry is not PET-09, because steam-mobilized bitumen already flows, and it is not PET-06, because the product is liquid crude.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The narrowed historical upgrading claim describes a distinct field result that the notes say still does not exist.
